achievers.achievementSummary: Named author of Lane Genealogies Vol. I (1891); prolific New Hampshire genealogist who completed the volume from manuscripts of Deacon E. J. Lane and Rev. James P. Lane. Also authored Leonard Weeks, Folsom, Philbrick, and Edward Chapman genealogies.

bookEvidence.note: Signed preface; assumed pecuniary responsibility with committee; credited Fitts for Candia and Chester lines.

achievers.achievementSummary: Co-author on title page; NEHGR member from 1867; antiquarian research for Candia and Chester Lane lines. Authored History of Newfields and Fitts family genealogy; posthumously completed Lane Genealogies Vol. III (1902).

bookEvidence.note: Chapman credits his accurate writing and antiquarian researches.
Frontispiece portrait Rev. Jas. H. Fitts

achievers.achievementSummary: Prior compiler; twenty years gathering Lane families; published in NEHGR (1873 abstract, 1888) and pamphlets including James Lane of North Yarmouth (1888). Manuscript passed to Chapman unfinished.

achievers.achievementSummary: Resumed family genealogy in 1839; collected records for 30+ years; furnished NEHGR abstract April 1873 (four generations, five pages). Operated Lane's Bookstore in Dover (1832–1899 family business). Subject of extended preface sketch.

bookEvidence.note: Chapman 'specimens of Lane character' sketch; manuscript placed in Chapman's hands.

achievers.achievementSummary: Farmer, surveyor, shoemaker, tanner, deacon; Stratham town clerk from 1774. His diaries and journals are classic New Hampshire Revolutionary-era primary sources, published by NHHS.

achievers.achievementSummary: Mexican-American War veteran and Forty-niner; first permanent settler on the Mojave River; founded Lane's Crossing (1858–65) on the Mormon Road — the Last Crossing before Cajon Pass.
achievers.detailLead: Piermont, N.H. farmer turned frontier station-keeper at the Lower Narrows ford where Mormon Road, Mojave Road, and Mohave Trail traffic converged.
detailBullets: Co. H, 9th U.S. Infantry (1847–48); malaria at Puebla; California Gold Rush by 1850.
Lane's Crossing ranch & store — first settlement on the Mojave River; sold 1865 for Bryman alfalfa ranch.
Twin Moses Lane died at Acapulco en route to California; niece Eldora Richmond nursed Aaron at Halleck, 1883.
achievers.bookQuote: XV. CAPT. AARON G.⁶ (twin brother to Moses), b. 23 Dec., 1817, went to California in 1849… died unm. 14 Sept., 1883, at Lane's Crossing of the Mojave river.

galleryImages.alt: Mojave River Narrows near Victorville, ca. 1905
galleryImages.caption: Lower Narrows — Lane's Crossing ford

bookEvidence.note: Went to California 1849; widely known in early Mojave corridor; Mrs. Richmond niece at Halleck.
Twin Moses P. Lane d. Acapulco 1852; dau. Eldora m. George Richmond.
